I'm 45, and after finishing my diploma at the agricultural technical college in Handan, I came back to take over the family land in Anzhai Township. I manage 10 mu of good flatland that my father and I have worked for decades. Last October I rotary-tilled the full field and sowed Shimai 22, an improved wheat variety, at about 25 jin per mu. I applied basal compound fertilizer then, so right now my focus is on spring management.

For the wheat that's already in the ground, I've learned from the county extension trainings that the recommended pure nitrogen rate for our soil type is around 15–18 kg per mu, but I've also seen my neighbor cut back to 15 kg last year and his yield dropped to 900 kg/mu while I applied 20 kg and got 1,050 kg. I'm targeting 1,050 kg/mu again this year. I'll apply one topdressing of urea at jointing stage to bring my total nitrogen to about 20 kg/mu. For phosphorus and potassium, I'm applying roughly 8 kg P₂O₅ and 3 kg K₂O through the basal compound — our soil is medium in phosphorus and I don't want to over-apply like some farmers who just dump on compound fertilizer. I'll irrigate four times: the green-up water now in early spring, jointing water in April, booting water in early May, and one grain-filling irrigation if May turns dry. Pumping from the tube well costs about 50 yuan per mu each time, so 200 yuan for water alone, but I've seen what drought at grain-filling does — it's not worth the risk. For crop protection, I'll spray herbicide once at the three-leaf stage, two rounds of insecticide for aphids, and one fungicide at heading — four applications total.

After wheat harvest in mid-June, I'll immediately plant Denghai 605 hybrid maize using no-tillage direct seeding. The turnaround window is only about five to seven days, so there's no time for ploughing — I'll hire the custom seeder to plant right into the wheat stubble. I'll apply 60 kg/mu of 28-6-6 compound as basal fertilizer, then topdress with urea at the large喇叭口 stage. That gives me about 18 kg N, 5 kg P₂O₅, and 4 kg K₂O per mu for the maize. I'll irrigate twice — once at joint stage and once at filling — since July usually brings some rain. Three pesticide applications: one pre-emergence herbicide and two insecticide sprays for corn borer. I'm expecting about 1,200 kg/mu from the maize.

I thought about converting 2 mu to vegetables like watermelon or chili for higher profit, but my wife works part-time in the county town and my son is away at university, so I don't have the labor for the intensive management vegetables require. The wheat-maize double crop is my anchor — the market is stable, I understand the inputs, and even if prices dip one season, the other usually carries us through.

decision.reasoning_summary: I manage 10 mu in Anzhai Township with a wheat-maize double-cropping system because it balances stable grain markets with manageable labor requirements for my household. I target 20 kg N/mu for wheat and 18 kg N/mu for maize based on extension recommendations adjusted upward slightly from loss aversion, with P and K tailored to our medium-P soil. I irrigate wheat four times and maize twice, matching the local groundwater-based border irrigation practice. I chose improved wheat and hybrid maize varieties with proven local performance, and I use no-tillage for maize because the five-to-seven-day planting window after wheat harvest makes ploughing impossible.
